HotPlate es una estación de soldadura de: HotPlate is a soldering station for SMD Electronics Component, free and with open hardware and software. A 4-ramp profile, predictive PID control with autotune, USB with AT commands and the HotPlate Studio app to calibrate it.

Gratis y abierto. Firmware y HotPlate St: Free and open. Firmware and HotPlate Studio under **MIT**, board and enclosure under **CERN-OHL-P-2.0** and documentation under **CC BY 4.0**. It runs on mains power and gets very hot, so handle it with care.
Hecha para ingenieros electrónicos, estu: Made for electronics engineers, students and hobbyists who want to solder SMD Electronics Component with a real temperature profile. It has predictive **PID** control, a **USB** link and an app to calibrate it. It's free and open, so you can build it and adapt it to whatever you need.
Armas tu perfil, pulsas RUN y HotPlate s: Set up your profile, press RUN and HotPlate takes care of the rest
Un perfil de soldadura tiene hasta cuatr: A soldering profile has up to four ramps, each with its temperature and how long it should stay there. HotPlate runs through them in order, doses the power so it doesn't overshoot, and at the end turns the heat off, lets you know and cools down with air. What you see below is a real cycle recorded on the test bench, with the same screen the device has.

Ciclo real de cuatro rampas, de 100 a 13: Real four-ramp cycle, from 100 to 130 °C. Sped up ×16 while heating and ×120 while cooling.
A cada rampa le pones temperatura y tiem: Give each ramp a temperature and a soak time, and the cycle runs on its own from start to finish. Ramps only go up or stay level, and if you want to stop, just hit **STOP**.
Calcula hacia dónde va la temperatura en: It works out where the temperature is heading over the next 15 s and lowers the power before it gets there. That way the plate doesn't go past what you asked for.
Con el autoajuste, HotPlate hace unas cu: With autotune, HotPlate runs a few oscillations, measures how your plate responds and computes its own gains. They're saved on the device.
Conéctala al computador y manéjala desde: Plug it into your computer and drive it from HotPlate Studio or your own script. Every second it sends you temperature, phase and power.
Segura desde que la enciendes: Safe from the moment you turn it on
Arranca siempre con el calor apagado. Si: It always boots with the heat off. If the sensor fails, if it goes over the maximum temperature or if it can't reach the setpoint, it cuts off and lets you know.
Déjala lista y que arranque sola hasta 1: Leave it ready and let it start on its own up to 12 hours later. When it's done it beeps and blows air so it cools faster.

Una placa caliente tiene inercia y, si c: A hot plate has inertia, and if you cut the heat right when it arrives it keeps climbing a few degrees. That's why HotPlate's **predictive PI** looks 15 s ahead and eases off the power early. These numbers come from real runs with the current firmware.

Contrólala desde tu propio código: Control it from your own code
Además de Studio, HotPlate entiende **co: Besides Studio, HotPlate understands **AT commands** over USB. With five commands (`MODE`, `RUN`, `STOP`, `CFG` and `STAT`) you load the profile, start the cycle and check the status, and every second you get a line with temperature, phase and power.
Te sirve para meterla en un script de Py: Use it in a Python script, a test bench or a small production line. While you drive it over USB, the integrated **HotPanel** stays locked.
# Una línea por comando; lo que sigue a:
# One line per command; anything after # is a comment and is not sent.
AT+MODE=1            # take control (HotPanel shows USB)
AT+CFG=R,0,150,120   # step 1: 150 °C, 120 s
AT+CFG=R,1,165,90    # step 2: 165 °C, 90 s
AT+CFG=R,2,175,60    # step 3: 175 °C, 60 s
AT+CFG=H,0,1         # no wait, air at the end
AT+RUN=1             # start HEAT → OK
$HP,T=119.6,P=1,A=5,SET=130,DLY=0,RUN=30:
$HP,T=119.6,P=1,A=5,SET=130,DLY=0,RUN=30,EL=311,DU=61,F=0,RI=3,FL=0

# T    temperature (°C)       A   phase: 5 = rising, 4 = soak
# SET  setpoint (°C)          RUN time left in the phase (s)
# EL   elapsed (s)            DU  heater power (%)
# RI   current step           FL  fault 0/1
AT+MODE=1\nAT+RUN=2,150,5,15,1200\n\n# 1:
AT+MODE=1
AT+RUN=2,150,5,15,1200

# 150 °C, 5 cycles, ±1.5 °C hysteresis, 1200 s maximum.
# The $HP frame adds AP (phase), AC (cycles), AK and AI (gains).
# When it finishes, Kp and Ki are written to EEPROM on their own.
El cerebro es un ATmega16 con 16 KB de m: The brain is an ATmega16 with 16 KB of memory. At the same time it reads the sensor, works out the power, advances the profile, updates the screen and answers over USB, without one task holding up the others.

¿Puedo fabricar y modificar la mía?: Can I build and modify my own?
¡Claro que sí! Para eso está todo public: Of course! That's why everything is published. Download the files, build it your way and, if you improve it, share your changes so others can use them too. Just keep in mind that it plugs into mains power, so take your time and ask for help if it's your first time with those voltages.
¿Necesito el computador para usarla?: Do I need a computer to use it?
No. Desde el **HotPanel integrado** edit: No. From the integrated **HotPanel** you edit the four ramps and the start time, and start the cycle. You need HotPlate Studio to calibrate it and to change limits, bands and gains, and all of that is saved on the device.
¿Sirve para soldadura sin plomo?: Does it work for lead-free solder?
El firmware acepta hasta 250 °C, pero ha: The firmware accepts up to 250 °C, but so far the published tests reach 171.7 °C. The documented profile is for Sn63/Pb37, which melts at 183 °C. For lead-free (≈ 217 °C) you first need to check that your plate gets there under load.
Se apagan el calefactor y el aire, y el: The heater and the air turn off and the device goes into fault. The same happens if the temperature hits the configured maximum (`ERROR:7`) or if it can't reach the setpoint (`ERROR:9`).
